guard: pi's cotal_send returns the shared refusal for a pattern or a name that is no channel, without touching the mesh agent
why: pi registers the shared tool specs, so it advertises the shared channel text. Its wrapper used
to answer a pattern first with its own "is not a concrete channel" line, so a pi session never
saw the two ways to reach a family that the text promises.
PS1 puts that wrapper check back.
PS2 stops dropping a leading #, so #team.> reaches the shared check as a name that is no channel.
NO BUILD STEP: the suite imports ../src/tools.js.

mutations.name: PS1 pi refuses a non-concrete channel with its own line before the shared handler
mutations.expectRed: pi refuses team.> with the shared pattern refusal, naming both ways
mutations.cell: pi refuses team.> with the shared pattern refusal, naming both ways
mutations.note: The cold review's live defect: the pi wrapper's own line, with neither way to reach a family.

mutations.name: PS2 pi stops dropping a leading # before the shared check
mutations.expectRed: pi drops a leading # before the shared check, so #team.** is refused as "team.**"
mutations.cell: pi drops a leading # before the shared check, so #team.** is refused as "team.**"
mutations.note: A model that echoes the display # back would be told its channel is no channel name.
